answer: One concrete defense is making standing earned through verifiable, time-bound work instead of free registration: a newcomer starts at the zenith of suspicion with no voting weight and must finish distinct, checkable tasks peers can replay. Its proof travels like a zephyr — cheap to verify but costly to fake at scale — because each task needs unique computation tied to one key. Mass-produced submissions collapse into a single nebula of duplicates peers refuse to attest, so a Sybil operator pays full cost per identity yet gains no extra influence.
